name: Bonanza Peak and Martin Peak from Holden Pass

legs.route: Mary Green Glacier to the northeast ridge

legs.connect: Return to the Holden Pass camp, then head up the broad ridge of Martin, the same afternoon or the next morning.

how: Both peaks are climbed from one camp just below Holden Pass. Bonanza goes first as the bigger day: waterfall slabs, a rope-up on the Mary Green Glacier, then rock with a no-fall crux around class 4 to low 5th and mostly class 3 elsewhere. Martin is shorter but loose and chossy, ending in two short class 4 variations on the summit block. Beyond Bonanza alone, the link adds only time and a second summit push.
descent: Bonanza is downclimbed along the ascent line back to camp, usually without rope. Martin takes one rappel off the summit and then careful downclimbing, followed by the walk back to the pass.
logistics: The usual way in, by lake ferry to Lucerne and the village bus to Holden, is shut: storm damage closed the road from Lucerne to all traffic, by an order that runs through 2027, and the village is closed to guests. Until it reopens, the Holden Lake trail can only be reached from the west or north over Cloudy Pass, which adds days. Go in summer, once the glacier is open and the slabs are free of ice.
notes: Sources disagree on the Bonanza crux (class 4 vs low 5th); higher kept. A Dark Peak to Bonanza ridge traverse that finishes with Martin from Holden Pass also exists (one source only, not entered). A search snippet mentioned a 2025 fire closure of the Bonanza trail; I did not read it, so no closure is stated in the prose; check current status. 2026-10-30 (session): Holden access closure verified on holdenvillage.org hiker services (July 8 2026 release; FSR 8301 closure order to 2027-12-31) and WTA Holden Lake alert 6.9.26; logistics rewritten.

name: Glacier Peak and Kololo Peak from Glacier Gap

legs.route: Across the glacier to the south face and south ridge (snow and rock)
Gerdine / South Ridge via the Disappointment Peak col
legs.connect: From the Glacier Gap camp, usually the next day: climb to the col above Disappointment Peak and follow the south ridge to the summit.

how: Both summits are done from one high camp at Glacier Gap. Kololo (about 8,200 ft) is the easy outing, over the Suiattle or White Chuck Glacier to a short snow and rock finish; treat the glacier as real glacier travel. Glacier Peak (10,541 ft) takes its own day with crampons and glacier gear, over the col above Disappointment Peak and up the south ridge. In spring, skis cover much of the way.
descent: Retrace the south ridge to camp. The walk out is long, crossing toward Foam Basin or White Pass and then down to the North Fork Sauk road.
logistics: A cross-country approach from the North Fork Sauk road to Glacier Gap makes a long first day, so plan three to four days. Both the spring ski and summer snow seasons work; expect strong wind on the col.
notes: Order differs between reports (Kololo first in the spring ski trip; Glacier Peak first in the summer loop, which came from the Kennedy Glacier side). Disappointment Peak is a side summit near the col, not entered as a leg. A further source (a 2012 circuit report) was blocked.

name: Mount Mystery, Hal Foss Peak and Fricaba from Deception Basin
region: Olympic Mountains (Royal Basin and Deception Basin)

legs.route: Snow and rock from Deception Basin, loose class 3 to class 4 finish
Snow slopes or small glacier, then a short ridge scramble (mostly class 2)
legs.connect: Cross Deception Basin to the slopes of Hal Foss, the same evening after Mystery or the next morning.

legs.route: Ridge from the Hal Foss saddle
legs.connect: Drop to the saddle and follow the ridge, roughly 45 minutes.

how: Hike into Royal Basin, cross the notch into Deception Basin and camp there. Mystery is the hard peak of the trio: loose class 3 to 4 with rockfall, best while snow still covers the approaches. Hal Foss and Fricaba are easy by comparison and are often done together the next morning. The trio adds snow travel in the basin and a pass crossing between two drainages.
descent: Drop the northwest ridge of Fricaba, cross the saddles toward Milk Creek and return to upper Royal Basin. A saddle north of the basin lake, past the tarns toward Royal Lake, also works.
logistics: Start at the Dungeness trailhead; Royal Lake is under three hours in. An overnight wilderness permit is needed. Snow in late spring or early summer makes Mystery and the passes safer; late season is loose.
notes: Fricaba's class is not stated. Mystery is also done alone via the Mystery Glacier (class 3 grade II per a guide cited in an older report). Another report climbed Mystery and Deception instead of Hal Foss and Fricaba (one source only).
